correctness.rationale: The nonzero bounded functional admits an H^p extremizer; Brevig–Søvik 2026 proves every such extremizer outer for p<1, hence a zero-free analytic q=2/p power root h in H². Taylor algebra a0=a^q and a2=qa^(q-1)c+[q(q-1)/2]a^(q-2)b² and Parseval yield a sharp upper bound over x²+y²+w²<=1. At fixed x the objective is strictly concave in w and its unique optimizer is min(x/(q-1),sqrt(1-x²)); derivative signs in the two x regimes prove the global bifurcation at tau=1/(q-2). Schur stability gives the displayed zero-free quadratic powers so equality is realized, while phase rigidity eliminates other extremizers. Supporting-plane inequalities and continuity give the claimed fixed-origin range and endpoints; the earlier exact Phi1 theorem applies throughout t>=tstar, and the positive-square gap below tstar proves sharpness. A separate scan of 30 support profiles against 90k constrained real-slice values matched the formulas; that finite scan does not prove the Hardy-space reduction or global derivative signs.

originality.rationale: Brevig–Grepstad–Instanes (2022 journal, Theorem 12 and Question 2) compute Phi1 for every p<1, expressly ask terminal equality for k>=2, and numerically anticipate the k=2 threshold; they leave a one-zero competitor unexcluded. Brevig–Søvik (Oct 2026) prove outer extremality for every bounded functional, a genuine necessary premise but without the mixed support norm or coefficient frontier. Brevig–Saksman gives unconditional individual coefficient norms. A published Resultary H^(1/2) special-case already proves the p=1/2 slice and is credited; the present full interval 0<p<1, including noninteger q, is not implied by that slice. Full independent priority certification is impossible, but the new all-exponent closed profile and proof are not covered by inspected sources.
